messages:
Alicia: Heads-up — we need a concrete proposal for the inspect/unmask UX + quota model before we ship the temporary debug flow next week. current blockers: quota exhaustion, audit trail, and PII risk.
Ryan: +1. can we make inspect tokens quota-backed instead of global? per-tenant short TTL tokens that require justification.
Sam: per-tenant quota sounds right. also we should auto-fallback to redacted traces when quota runs out rather than 500ing.
Alicia: proposed rules: 1) Inspect tokens issued via API or Console request, 2) token TTL default 1 hour, 3) each token consumes from tenant.inspect_quota, 4) if quota exhausted route to redacted variant.
Priya: product ask — the console flow needs a lightweight justification field on issue and an audit entry we can surface to compliance. can we make that required for >1h tokens?
Alicia: yes — justification required for TTL > 15m. audit entry must include hashed request id, who requested, and reason. store audit metadata in encrypted store (KMS).
Sam: implementation detail: do NOT store raw tenant IDs in logs. use HMAC(tenant_id, per-org-salt) for metrics keys so dashboards can correlate but not reveal PII.
Ryan: thinking about the routing policy: route = if inspect_token.valid and tenant.inspect_quota>0 -> full_trace_path else -> redacted_trace_path. Also add a burst allowance for SRE 'breakglass' tokens.
Mia: can we implement a sliding window for quota instead of simple counters? e.g., 100 inspect seconds per 1h per tenant. simpler for enforcement, avoids losing tokens across restarts.
Sam: yes sliding window makes sense. enforcement lives in the routing proxy so the path decision happens before payload is materialized. we should also instrument latency for the check (<1ms target).
Priya: console UX notes: show remaining quota, next refill time, and last 5 audit requests in a flyout. add a prominent banner when quota < 10% with a request button to raise quota (internal workflow).
Alicia: telemetry/dashboarding: we need metrics: inspect_requests_total, inspect_bytes_unmasked, inspect_quota_consumed, inspect_fallbacks_to_redacted. set alert if fallback rate > 5% for a tenant over 15m.
Ryan: also add a sampled log event for each unmask with hmac_id, route, dev_email, and reason truncated to 200 chars. sampled at 100% for audit bucket, 1% for general telemetry.
Sam: sampling strategy — we should tag audit bucket logs so they are retained longer and excluded from general analytics pipelines. redact any freeform user prompt content in telemetry unless explicitly requested in justification.
Mia: security question — how do we handle replay risk? if someone steals a token they could unmask data during TTL. maybe bind token to requester IP or session id and include short nonce.
Alicia: agree. bind tokens to the console session ID and optionally to a requester IP CIDR for 1h tokens. breakglass tokens can skip IP binding but need two-person approval.
Priya: for the console, implement a request modal: duration dropdown (15m, 1h, 4h), justification text, checkbox acknowledging audit. show estimated quota consumption before confirm.
Sam: dev note: small config snippet for the router enforcement: 
```
inspect_policy:
  ttl_default: 3600
  ttl_max: 14400
  per_tenant_quota: 600 # seconds per hour
  fallback_route: /v1/trace/redacted
  audit_sample_rate: 1.0 # audit bucket
  telemetry_sample_rate: 0.01
```
Alicia: can infra-bot remind infra to cut a small canary for this? want to dogfood in staging for two days. @infra-bot? :eyes:
infra-bot: deploy scheduled — canary "inspect-quota-canary" rolling to staging at 2026-03-24T21:00Z. monitor inspect_fallbacks and audit events.
Ryan: post-canary checklist: validate sliding-window counters across restarts, confirm HMAC key rotation plan, verify KMS encryption for audit store, and run privacy review.
Mia: one more: add a CLI path to request inspect tokens for automation but require service account justify metadata and org admin approval.
Alicia: thanks all — I'll draft the RFC with the policy, console mocks, and the router config. will ping for review tomorrow. :thumbsup:
